title: Telemetry-driven compile bundles and fallback policy for composite attention models
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Create a telemetry-driven system that builds per-model compile bundles (signed profile + kernel ordering + fallback graph) for composite attention architectures (MHA, GQA, MoE). These bundles will be published to the model catalog and can be pinned by model version. The system must generate reproducible bundles from representative workload traces, include a prioritized fallback sequence for degraded kernels, and expose rollout controls for staged publishing and automatic rollback.
goals: 1) Reduce variance in p95 token latency for newly onboarded large models by selecting stable compile paths automatically. 2) Provide deterministic, versioned profile bundles that can be pinned by model owners. 3) Enable safe canary rollouts with automatic performance/regression gates and graceful fallback to compatible compiled variants.
background_and_rationale: We onboard many models with composite attention patterns (sparse MoE, grouped GQA, multi-headed MHA) where a single compile path often underperforms on tail latency or fails on sharded topologies. Current onboarding is manual and slow; teams select kernels ad hoc and then iterate after observing production regressions. By deriving compile bundles from real telemetry (sequence-length histograms, kv cache reuse patterns, expert routing heatmaps), we can pick kernel orderings and compilation flags that match the workload profile and precompute safe fallback sequences when kernels are unsupported or degrade.
proposal: - Telemetry collection: augment onboarder to capture anonymized sequence-length distributions, prefix reuse ratio, top-k expert routing histograms (for MoE), and token emission clustering for the onboarding traces. - Bundle builder: translate telemetry into a 'bundle' (signed artifact) containing: (a) prioritized kernel list per op (b) compile flags and quantization hints (c) fallback graph linking compatible kernels and acceptable perf degradation thresholds (d) recommended runtime config (batching targets, kv cache TTL)
acceptance_criteria: - Bundle builder produces repeatable bundles from the same trace and marks them with semantic version. - CI gate validates bundle in a small cluster: runs 5 canonical eval prompts and checks p50/p95 latency and token cost against baseline (<=5% regression p50, <=10% p95). - Console shows bundle version next to model in catalog and supports 'pin bundle' + 'rollback to previous bundle'. - Canary rollout API supports traffic split and automatic rollback on SLA trigger (p95 > baseline * 1.10 or error rate > 0.5%). - Documented onboarder flow and runbook for manual intervention.
tasks:
- Instrument onboarding harness to export telemetry (ENG-1)
- Implement bundle builder service (proto + signing) (ENG-2)
- Add CI perf gate job and synthetic runner (ENG-3)
- Console: bundle listing + pin/rollback controls (PM/UX ticket) (ENG-4)
- Runtime: implement bundle lookup and fallback executor (ENG-5)
- Create rollout automation with rollback triggers and alerting (ENG-6)
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: telemetry traces are not representative -> Mitigation: require minimum trace size and sample variance checks; fall back to conservative default bundle. - Risk: signed bundle pins may block fast patches -> Mitigation: allow emergency hotfix bundles with expedited CI and audit log. - Risk: fallback path causes correctness differences -> Mitigation: require function-level golden tests in CI to catch regressions.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for bundle builder transformations. - Integration test: onboard small model with synthetic MoE routing and validate fallback graph. - Canary test: rollout to 2% traffic for 24h with dedicated synthetic load and compare p50/p95 against baseline dashboards. - A/B experiment to measure token-cost delta over 7 days.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal only onboarding (engineering-owned) for 2 weeks. Phase 2: opt-in public catalog models with PM approval. Phase 3: default for new model onboardings after 6 weeks of observation and two successful canaries. Rollback policy: automatic on SLA trigger or manual from Console. Audit logs stored for every bundle publish/rollout.
metrics_to_track:
- p50 token latency (ms)
- p95 token latency (ms)
- error-rate (percent)
- tokens-per-second throughput
- cost-per-token (USD)
- number of automatic rollbacks
- bundle churn (publishes per model per month)
